data.name: Corinne Cross's Dead & Breakfast
data.detailed_description:
With no plans lined up after graduating, Corinne agrees to do a favor and look after a hospitalized acquaintance's home... a home that turns out to be a ghost-infested bed & breakfast! Her peaceful week of housesitting becomes seven days of madness as she finds herself surrounded by a variety of eccentric ghosts with entirely different demands...

Gameplay

  • Sidescrolling adventure game (NOT a horror game despite the ghosts)
  • A character-rich, story-driven experience
  • You have 7 days at the B&B. Try to make each day count!
  • Switches between day and night, affecting available interactions

Key Features

  • Gardening! Raise a garden by tending to the B&B's potted plants. Sell the flowers you've grown for money!
  • Cooking! Create tasty breakfast dishes in the kitchen. Can you find all 10 recipes?
  • Ghosts! Get to know the B&B's otherwordly guests. Choose what you say carefully! There are multiple endings based on your decisions.
  • New Game+! Beat the game once to unlock a harder version of the game with alternate dialogue, bonus scenes, extra content, and a few... secrets...

CCD&B was initially developed in a month for the 2015 IGMC (and won grand prize). This is an updated version with improved art, more illustrations, better writing and implementation of multiple endings, new characters and maps, and more content and details in general.

Created by Cecilia Bishton. Hope this game brings you a little joy.

data.short_description: A story-driven adventure game about a haunted bed & breakfast. A dead & breakfast!

reviews.review:
Corinne Cross's Dead & Breakfast is a compact story-driven adventure that turns a haunted bed and breakfast into something unexpectedly cozy, funny, and heartfelt. Instead of relying on scares, the game treats its supernatural setting as the foundation for a character-focused story about responsibility, uncertainty, and forming connections with a very unusual collection of residents. Developed and published by bad chalk and created by Cecilia Bishton, it has the unmistakable personality of a small indie project that prioritizes charm and storytelling over mechanical complexity.

The story follows Corinne, a recent graduate who has no firm plans for what to do with her life. She agrees to watch over the home of a hospitalized acquaintance, believing she is signing up for an uneventful week of housesitting. That expectation disappears when she discovers that the building is actually a bed and breakfast occupied by ghosts. What follows is a seven-day adventure in which Corinne must deal with eccentric supernatural guests, learn more about their circumstances, and decide how she wants to respond to their various demands.

Despite the ghostly premise, this is not a horror game. Its atmosphere is much closer to a supernatural slice-of-life adventure, combining humor, emotional moments, mystery, and everyday activities. This distinction is important because players expecting dangerous spirits, elaborate survival mechanics, or frightening encounters will find something completely different. The ghosts are characters to understand rather than enemies to defeat. Their personalities and interactions provide much of the game's appeal.

The seven-day structure gives the adventure a steady sense of progression. Time alternates between day and night, and certain interactions depend on the current period. This encourages revisiting areas and paying attention to how the B&B changes as time passes. The setting is relatively small, but that intimacy works in the game's favor because players gradually become familiar with its rooms, routines, and residents.

There are also several lightweight activities beyond talking and exploring. Gardening allows Corinne to tend potted plants, grow flowers, and sell what she produces for money. Cooking provides another relaxing diversion, with ten breakfast recipes waiting to be discovered. These systems are deliberately straightforward rather than deep simulations. Their main purpose is to make life at the B&B feel interactive and provide a pleasant routine between major conversations and story developments.

Dialogue choices carry greater importance because decisions can influence how events unfold. Players need to consider how Corinne responds to the ghosts, with multiple endings providing consequences for the choices made during the week. This makes conversations more meaningful and adds replay value to an otherwise relatively short adventure. It also complements the protagonist's situation nicely, since the story is partly about navigating an uncertain period of her life and deciding how she handles the people, or spirits, around her.

Completing the game unlocks New Game+, which is more substantial than a simple replay option. It offers a harder variation of the experience alongside alternate dialogue, bonus scenes, additional material, and secrets. Combined with the multiple endings, this makes returning for another playthrough worthwhile, especially for players who become attached to the characters and want to discover scenes they missed previously.

The presentation has a colorful 2D style that matches the game's gentle personality. It does not depend on sophisticated visual effects, instead using its artwork and illustrations to give the characters and supernatural setting their identity. The game originally began as a project developed for the 2015 Indie Game Making Contest, where it won the grand prize. The commercial release expanded that foundation with improved artwork, additional illustrations, revised writing, new characters and maps, multiple endings, and other content.

Its biggest weakness is also a natural consequence of its focused design. The gardening and cooking mechanics are pleasant but shallow, exploration is limited in scope, and players primarily interested in mechanical challenges may find the experience too simple. Much of the enjoyment depends on reading conversations and becoming interested in the personalities of the ghosts. The seven-day format also means the adventure does not attempt to become an enormous narrative experience. However, its relatively short length prevents its simple systems from becoming overly repetitive.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially rated Playable rather than fully Verified. The game runs successfully on Steam Deck, its interface text is legible, the default graphics configuration performs well, and its functionality can be accessed using the default controller configuration. The main compromise is that some prompts may display mouse, keyboard, or non-Steam Deck controller icons. External Bluetooth or USB controllers can also require manually selecting the active controller. These are relatively minor inconveniences for a slow-paced narrative adventure, making handheld play a practical way to experience it.

Corinne Cross's Dead & Breakfast ultimately succeeds through personality rather than scale. Its combination of supernatural storytelling, eccentric characters, meaningful dialogue decisions, gardening, cooking, day-and-night interactions, multiple endings, and New Game+ gives the small adventure surprising substance. It is especially appealing for players who enjoy cozy narrative games and want a ghost story built around companionship and humor instead of fear.

It is a warm and memorable indie adventure whose modest mechanics are elevated by an unusual premise, likable atmosphere, meaningful choices, and thoughtful replay content. The Steam Deck Playable rating also makes it a good fit for portable sessions, provided players do not mind the occasional non-Deck control prompt.

Rating: 8/10
